originalTitle: Ralph Lauren shares jump 7% as shoppers in Asia, North America drive revenue beat
simplifiedContent: Ralph Lauren's sales were better than expected, which made their stock price go up by 7%. This happened because a lot of people, especially younger ones, in Asia and North America were buying their products. In Asia, sales grew by 24%, mainly because of strong sales in China, and in North America, sales increased by 13%. Because of this good news, Ralph Lauren now thinks they will make more money this year than they originally thought, which is why their stock price rose. This matters because it shows that the company is doing well and investors are becoming more confident in their ability to grow and make money.

originalTitle: Alphabet looks to raise up to $25 billion from latest bond sale: report
simplifiedContent: Alphabet, the company that owns Google, is trying to borrow a lot of money - between $20 and $25 billion - by selling bonds. This means they're essentially asking investors to lend them money, and in return, they'll pay back the loan with some extra interest. The company is doing this after its spending plans caused some concern, and it's choosing to borrow money instead of using its own savings. This is similar to what other big tech companies are doing, as they're all working on expensive artificial intelligence projects and need funds to support them. By borrowing money, Alphabet can fund its projects without using up its own cash.

originalTitle: Tata Sons faces continued listing uncertainty after RBI classification
simplifiedContent: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is closely watching Tata Sons, a big company in India, to make sure it follows the rules. This is happening because Tata Sons was previously involved in lending money, and the RBI wants to keep an eye on it. Even though Tata Sons paid off its debts and asked to stop being a lender about two years ago, the RBI still hasn't made a decision on its request. This delay is also affecting the charitable work and investments of Tata Trusts, which is connected to Tata Sons. The RBI will likely wait until it decides on Tata Sons' request before requiring the company to list its shares on the stock market.

originalTitle: SanDisk shares dive 14% after soft revenue forecast eclipses strong Q4 earnings
simplifiedContent: SanDisk, a company that makes computer storage products, recently released its financial results for the last quarter of the year. Even though the company made more money than expected, its stock price fell 14% because it predicted its future revenue won't be as strong as investors had hoped. The company actually had a great quarter, with $8.97 billion in revenue, thanks to big companies buying its products for artificial intelligence projects. This drop in stock price matters because it shows that investors are more focused on the company's future prospects than its current success. The stock price fell to $1,163 after the announcement, which means investors who own SanDisk stock lost some value.

originalTitle: Sebi to simplify rules, deepen markets, ramp up technology use in FY27
simplifiedContent: The head of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi), Tuhin Kanta Pandey, has announced plans to make rules simpler and easier to follow in the next financial year. This means that Sebi wants to reduce complexity and make it faster for companies to get approvals. Sebi also plans to use more technology to supervise the markets, which should help make the markets more efficient. This is important because it could make it easier for companies to raise money and for investors to buy and sell shares, which can help the stock market grow. By making these changes, Sebi aims to make the markets stronger and more attractive to investors.

originalTitle: US stocks mixed as investors await Iran deal details, Western Digital plunges 18.5%, Sandisk dips 11.3%
simplifiedContent: The US stock market is having a mixed day, meaning some stocks are going up and others are going down. The main indexes, which track the performance of the market, are showing small changes: the Dow Jones is up a bit, the S&P 500 is also up, but the Nasdaq is down. This caution might be because investors are waiting to hear more about a potential deal with Iran. Two notable stocks, Western Digital and Sandisk, had big drops, falling 18.5% and 11.3% respectively. Overall, the market is in a bit of a holding pattern, with investors waiting for more information before making big moves.
